title: Hearing Coleman Hawkins, Bix, Jack Teagarden and Jimmy Harrison
summary: Jackson recalls Stumpy Evans praising Hawkins in 1923 and white musicians like Bix and Teagarden at the Sunset, and Jimmy Harrison as king.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah, he's from Denver but he's been there.

His home was in Texas, but I lived in there. But lung trouble I think he died. But that boy was wonderful. He used to tell me, you should hear Coleman Hawkins. Now that must have been in 1923. You should hear Coleman Hawkins.
You should hear Coleman Hawkins. Yeah.

So Joe Oliver, now there's the whole, there's Bix Bydebeck, Tea Garden. I saw Bix Bydebeck. See I have some, I saw something where a whole lot of people didn't see it. And I'm great. Bix Bydebeck was a great trumpet player. They had a whole lot of great white musicians too. There was this boy, this client, this player, what was his name, from around Chicago here? Tex. Yeah, Tex was great. Now that was Art Castle. I played against Art Castle with Dennis Goodman out the midway. And Moksi was the trumpet player. Moksi. See, great. See what I'm talking about? At the sunset you could see Tea Garden, once in a while Mip Moe would be in town, Bix Bydebeck, Tish, Art Castle, they'd all be there in their tuxedas. They'd reserve a whole table. At the old Royal Garden and the sunset, they'd be there. Tea Garden, all those fellas would be there. Right there, listening to them fellas. I got a chance to see all them fellas. I didn't know who they were. There was no introduction or nothing like that. But later on seeing the pictures, I found out who they were. I heard Tea Garden, I always did love Tea Garden playing. Always did. And I'd like to know who they were, I'd ask who, that's Jack Tea Garden. I finally met Tea Garden. And I'm glad to meet Tea Garden, because Tea Garden up to the day plays great trombone. Now Jimmy Harrison, I never saw him but I heard him. He died when he was in the yard with Louis. He was great. He was the king at the time. He was really the king at the time, Jimmy Harrison. And then here comes Mip Moe. Now Mip Moe was playing before I ever played. Mip Moe and Red, not Red Nickles, it's Pennies, who was that? Yeah, Pennies, yeah. That was a nice bunch wasn't it? Yeah. That was a good bunch wasn't it?
